title: Time for Stock Taking: Whither Sangh Parivar?
byline: compiled and edited by Sita Ram Goel · Voice of India · 1997
lede: In July 1996, after the first BJP government fell after thirteen days, Dr. Shreerang Godbole, a Pune doctor and an RSS volunteer of seventeen years, told a seminar attended by Sangh leaders that their own slogans about Muslims were confused. Voice of India circulated his two documents as an eight-page brochure in October 1996 and invited responses. This book collects them: essays by David Frawley and Goel, then 47 replies from Hindu professionals, academics and Sangh workers.
facts: Godbole's time as an RSS swayamsevak
responses printed, nearly all agreeing with him
the Prajna Bharati seminar in Pune where he spoke, with K.S. Sudarshan, M.M. Joshi and others present
note: This is an argument within the Hindu nationalist movement, from its harder-line wing. The responses Voice of India printed are mostly supportive. The guide summarises the debate as recorded in the book.

sections.title: Eight formulations and Godbole's objections
head: Sangh Parivar formulation
Godbole's objection
rows: 1. What is the harm in adding Jesus and Muhammad to the 33 crore Hindu gods?
The question is whether Islam and Christianity accept any other god. They do not.
2. All religions, including Islam, lead to God.
Not all paths go up the mountain. He quotes David Frawley: some are “airplanes”, some “bullock carts”.
3. Islam is good but Muslims are bad.
“Quite the reverse”: Muslims without Islam are like anyone else. He argues the pre-Islamic Arabs and Turks were tolerant, and that it was Islam that hardened them.
4. Told of their common ancestry, Muslims will unite with Hindus.
Muslims know their ancestors converted. For them the pre-Islamic past is jahiliya, an age of darkness.
The reverse again: Muslims used the Congress, then dropped it for the Third Front and voted tactically against the BJP.
“The most fanatic of Muslims”. He cites Shah Waliullah, and Eaton's Sufis of Bijapur.
Not the leaders but the theology, which in his reading tells Muslims to keep apart from unbelievers.
8. Namaz on a disputed site is not acceptable to Allah.
“Plain nonsense”: nothing in the Quran or Hadis says so. He compares assimilating Muslims into the BJP/RSS to assimilating Marxists.

sections.title: The Sarva Panth Samadar Manch
items: Godbole objects to the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh's “platform for equal honour to all ways of worship”.
The BMS founder, who invited a maulana to Dr. Hedgewar's samadhi (memorial). Goel's appendix attacks this.
The Congress had taken Hindus for granted since 1885, and he warns the Sangh is following the same path.

sections.title: Some of the 47 who replied
sections.lede: Academics, doctors, engineers, retired officials and Sangh workers. Most agree with Godbole. A few, like G.V. Ashtekar, add qualifications.
